                                                   Sahil Bhola∗

                                       Last Edited: September 10, 2026



1        Floating-Point Model
We assume the standard floating-point model [1]: for every elementary operation ◦ ∈ {+, −, ×, /},
                                      fl(a ◦ b) = (a ◦ b)(1 + δ),   |δ| ≤ u,                       (1)
where u is the unit roundoff and δ is the relative roundoff error. Using eq. (1) for numerical analysis
we typicall obtain the product
                                Yn
                                    (1 + δi )ρi ≜ 1 + θn ,    ρ = ±1,                               (2)
                                       i=1
where n denotes the number of accumulated roundoff error terms. For numerical analysis, we seek
reliable and sharp bounds for θn .


2        Deterministic Rounding Error Analysis
The deterministic rounding error analysis proposes the following problem-size dependent constant
                                                  nu
                                          γn ≜         ,                                      (3)
                                                1 − nu
for nu < 1. Here, n is the number of accumulated error terms [1]. The problem-size dependent
constant is monotonic, that is, γn+1 > γn for u > 0. Performing backward/forward error analysis
using eq. (3) we obtain
                                                     |θn | ≤ γn .                                  (4)

such that y = S1ℓ . Here, ℓ† ≜ ⌈log2 n⌉ and Si0 = xi for all i. Note that, for some values of ℓ and n,

     3	/-! Offset-paired binary reduction from Bhola, Algorithm 1.
     4	Input occurrences carry their original indices. A carry creates no rounding node.

    13	def Tree.leaves : Tree → List (ℕ × ℝ)

    15	  | .add _ _ a b => a.leaves ++ b.leaves
    16

    21	/-- Pair left slot k with right slot k, whose original offset is the split size.
    22	If the right slot is absent, return the left tree literally unchanged. -/
    23	def pair (level : ℕ) : ℕ → List Tree → List Tree → List Tree
    24	  | _, [], ys => ys
    25	  | _, xs, [] => xs
    26	  | k, a :: as, b :: bs => .add level k a b :: pair level (k + 1) as bs

    31	def step (n level : ℕ) (ts : List Tree) : List Tree :=
    32	  pair level 0 (ts.take (offset n level)) (ts.drop (offset n level))
    33	
    34	def rounds (n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ → List Tree → List Tree
    35	  | 0, _, ts => ts

    43	    (xs.zipIdx.map fun p => Tree.leaf p.2 p.1)

    46	  | .leaf _ x => x

   323	theorem theorem_3_1 (xs : List ℝ) (hne : xs ≠ []) (u : ℝ)
   324	    (δ : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (hv : ValidErrors u δ)
